## **Setup Context and Problem**


I am following the steps in tutorial.md to run the tutorial simulation. While running the command


`alpasim_wizard +deploy=local wizard.log_dir=$PWD/tutorial`

or, directly the `run.sh` inside the `tutorial` directory using - `bash run.sh`

the image build fails at the uv sync step while fetching:

`git+https://github.com/valeoai/VideoActionModel.git`

Git fails with a TLS handshake error.

## **Command**

`alpasim_wizard +deploy=local wizard.log_dir=$PWD/tutorial`

```

RUN --mount=type=secret,id=netrc,target=/home/ubuntu/.netrc \
```

comments.body:
Can you pull it outside of the docker build? I.e. with `git clone https://github.com/valeoai/VideoActionModel.git`?
If yes, can you try running 
```
alpasim_wizard +deploy=local wizard.log_dir=$PWD/tutorial wizard.debug_flags.use_localhost=True
```

Thanks a lot for your time and the reply. I was able to resolve the issue by enabling host networking in the Docker Compose files and building the containers directly via `run.sh` from the terminal in both `tutorial` and `tutorial_alpamayo` folders. After this change, I was able to successfully build and run the containers, though i am not sure this is the correct approach. I will also try the solution you have suggested. However, when switching to **Alpamayo** (which is my main goal), I am consistently running into a different problem. The simulation fails at runtime with a **CUDA Out-Of-Memory error in `sensorsim`**. This occurs initially and causes secondary errors like `Session does not exist`. So while **VaVaM** runs correctly on my setup, **Alpamayo** appears to hit significantly higher GPU memory usage during rendering. --- ## What Works - Docker images build successfully - Docker Compose starts all services - VaVaM model runs without issues - Physics, controller, runtime, and driver initialize correctly - Scene loads successfully ## What Fails - Alpamayo model rollout ## System Specifications - **GPU:** NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 (24 GB VRAM) - **CUDA version:** 13.1 - **OS:** Ubuntu 24.04.3 (x86_64) ## Error Log ``` runtime-0-1 | } runtime-0-1 | } runtime-0-1 | (session=c173f164-f69f-11f0-a2a3-167dba5579dd, service_addr=sensorsim-0:6001) sensorsim-0-1 | [2026-01-21 08:04:23,674][nre.grpc.serve][INFO] render_rgb sensorsim-0-1 | [2026-01-21 08:04:24,181][grpc._server][ERROR] Exception calling application: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 508.00 MiB. GPU 0 has a total capacity of 23.56 GiB of which 216.75 MiB is free. Including non-PyTorch memory, this process has 1.70 GiB memory in use. Of the allocated memory 1.37 GiB is allocated by PyTorch, and 24.51 MiB is reserved by PyTorch but unallocated. If reserved but unallocated memory is large try setting PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True to avoid fragmentation. See documentation for Memory Management (https://pytorch.org/docs/stable/notes/cuda.html#environment-variables) ``` Which further raises errors like: ``` runtime-0-1 | File "/repo/src/runtime/alpasim_runtime/loop.py", line 815, in _loop controller-0-1 | KeyError: 'Session c173f164-f69f-11f0-a2a3-167dba5579dd does not exist' sensorsim-0-1 | File "/app/pycena_run.runfiles/pip_deps_3_11_grpcio/site-packages/grpc/_server.py", line 609, in _call_behavior runtime-0-1 | await asyncio.gather(*tasks) sensorsim-0-1 | response_or_iterator = behavior(argument, context) runtime-0-1 | File "/repo/src/runtime/alpasim_runtime/loop.py", line 746, in _send_images sensorsim-0-1 | ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ runtime-0-1 | await asyncio.gather( sensorsim-0-1 | File "nre/utils/", line 0, in wrapper sensorsim-0-1 | File "nre/grpc/", line 0, in render_rgb runtime-0-1 | File "/repo/src/runtime/alpasim_runtime/loop.py", line 460, in render_and_send_image sensorsim-0-1 | torch.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 508.00 MiB. GPU 0 has a total capacity of 23.56 GiB of which 216.75 MiB is free. Including non-PyTorch memory, this process has 1.70 GiB memory in use. Of the allocated memory 1.37 GiB is allocated by PyTorch, and 24.51 MiB is reserved by PyTorch but unallocated. If reserved but unallocated memory is large try setting PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True to avoid fragmentation. See documentation for Memory Management (https://pytorch.org/docs/stable/notes/cuda.html#environment-variables) runtime-0-1 | image = await self.sensorsim.render( sensorsim-0-1 | This can occur when running an unconverged checkpoint, or when volumetric effects are present (.e.g fog). sensorsim-0-1 | [2026-01-21 08:04:24,197][nre.grpc.serve][INFO] render_rgb runtime-0-1 | ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ sensorsim-0-1 | [2026-01-21 08:04:24,197][nre.grpc.serve][INFO] Creating new backend for clipgt-05bb8212-63e1-40a8-b4fc-3142c0e94646 from /mnt/nre-data/scenesets/2ecd7b86f6a864127b8bbecbff539872/318cf863-25ea-4d9b-b3b4-e4eb902bf69d.usdz runtime-0-1 | response: RGBRenderReturn = await profiled_rpc_call( runtime-0-1 | ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ runtime-0-1 | File "/repo/src/runtime/alpasim_runtime/telemetry/rpc_wrapper.py", line 124, in profiled_rpc_call runtime-0-1 | result = await fut runtime-0-1 | ^^^^^^^^^ runtime-0-1 | File "/repo/.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/grpc/aio/_call.py", line 328, in __await__ runtime-0-1 | raise _create_rpc_error( runtime-0-1 | grpc.aio._call.AioRpcError: ``` And the terminal is stuck after the below line, with a constant 5gb GPU memory usage. ``` sensorsim-0-1 | [2026-01-21 08:04:37,860][111IIIl11I1l1111l111lIllI][INFO] Model v$25.7.9 is already compatible with NuRec v25.7.9, no upgrade needed ``` I have also set the `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True` in the container environment, as listed in the error logs. **As a clarification** Is it possible to run Alpasim in a CPU-only mode instead of requiring a GPU, even if at reduced performance?

Great you fix it! My solution would have tried the same thing, `use_localhost=True` should enable the host network.

Re OOM error: Yes, I think 24 GB might just not be enough. I believe Alpamayo takes around that amount and sensorsim takes a couple more. 

Re running on CPU: I don't think anyone of us has tried that, so unfortunately can't help you. But even if you could get it to run, it will be _very_ slow!

Thanks for the quick reply, really appreciate it! I ran Alpamayo inference on CPU — it's slow but working. While doing this, I observe that the GPU usage for the containers is ~6 GB. So I guess running the full setup on GPU would need at least 32 GB VRAM. Is that right?

Nice, glad you got it running! And yes, 32GB sounds about right, though a couple of extra as buffer probably wouldn't hurt. 
Closing the issue but feel free to re-open.
